an1.296:1.1: Each of these terms has a specialized meaning; for example, disillusionment” (_nibbidā_) is the turning away in disappointment upon realizing that one cannot get what one wants ([mn50:31.15](), [sn35.240:1.8]()). But when used together they are all terms for Nibbana.
an1.296:1.3: The first six of these meditation topics are detailed in [an6.10]().
an1.297-305:1.3: The three mindfulness topics of breathing, body, and death are detailed especially in [mn10](), [mn118](), and [mn119](). | The “recollection of peace” (_upasamānussati_) is found only here (and at [an1.494]()), and is not further explained in early texts. Visuddhimagga 8.245–251 refers it to the recollection of Nibbāna at [an4.34:3.1]() and to the Asaṅkhatasaṁyutta ([sn43.1]() ff.). It also quotes a passage parallel to the phrase _tathāgataṁ ārabbha_ at [an6.10:2.5](), which is repeated with variations for each item of the six recollections. Visuddhimagga repeats the exact passage, except with _upasamaṁ ārabbha_ (“based on peace”). Since this is not found in the Pali canon today, it is likely this text has been lost, along with the explanation of the meditation.
